explanation: There is no base case: every call makes a new recursive call with n - 1, and nothing ever returns a value directly. The recursion never bottoms out, so the call stack grows without bound until Python raises RecursionError. The fix is to return 0 (or n) when n reaches a floor value.
prompt: What's the bug in this function that sums 1 through n?
choices: There is no base case, so it recurses forever and raises RecursionError
sum_to() is O(n^2) because each call re-scans the range
n - 1 overflows for large values of n
It should return n * sum_to(n - 1) instead
